hardwareHubs.note: Home to Quelab and the FUSE Makerspace, with the statewide NM MEP also based in the city.
MAKE Santa Fe is a community makerspace with CNC, laser and 3D printing equipment.

makerspaces.name: Quelab
makerspaces.note: Lists laser cutters, a CNC wood router, a CNC plasma cutter, a 3D printer lab and a machine shop.

makerspaces.name: FUSE Makerspace
makerspaces.note: Run with Central New Mexico Community College and lists CNC, laser, 3D printing and metalworking.

makerspaces.name: MAKE Santa Fe
makerspaces.note: Lists CNC routers, a CNC plasma cutter, laser cutters, 3D printers and an electronics station.

makerspaces.name: Cruces Creatives
makerspaces.note: Volunteer-run space listed with a woodshop, CNC machines, a milling machine and 3D printers.

events.name: Albuquerque Mini Maker Faire
events.note: Run by New Mexico New Makers, with editions reported from 2013 onward.

programs.name: Scale Up New Mexico (NMSU Arrowhead Center)
programs.note: Offers TechSprint accelerators, SBIR/STTR support and IP training for technology startups.

specialties.name: Optics and photonics
specialties.note: A 2014 state study counted 96 photonics firms producing about 8 percent of state manufacturing revenue.

specialties.name: Space, aerospace and defense
specialties.note: A state chamber foundation report names it a key sector projected to be the fastest growing over the next decade.

specialties.name: Quantum and advanced computing
specialties.note: The same report says the sector contributed about 6.5 billion dollars to the state economy in 2025.

support.name: New Mexico MEP
support.note: NIST MEP center in Albuquerque offering help with process improvement, product development and supply chain.
